ps to the matched message)
# dsh-session-keyword-search

Keyword search across **every** DeepSeek Harness session — the kind of search you
want when you reme
mber a phrase but not the conversation.

It takes over the sidebar search box instead of adding a second entry point: type
`大麦 x-sign` and th
e existing search lists the sessions that talked about it.
## Why this exists

The harness ships an SQLite FTS5 search behind `ctx.sessionQuery.searchSessions`.
Its tokenizer is `

unicode61`, so one contiguous CJK run is a **single token**:
a document containing `大麦协议劫持已在真机验证通过`

does not match `大麦`, and
`会话搜索` does not match `搜索`. This plugin replaces those two search methods
w
ith a substring index, so Chinese, English and mixed queries all behave the same.
## What it does

- **Substring recall.** `LIKE` over a lowercased text column: no tokenizer, no
phrase quoting rules

to remember, no minimum token length.
- **Session-level AND.** Whitespace separates terms; every ter

m must appear
somewhere in the session, but not necessarily in the same message. A quoted
`"phrase"`

must appear verbatim inside one message.
- **Ranked sessions.** More matching messages first, then

recent activity, with
the current workspace winning ties.
- **Provenance decides, not guessing.** Ev

ery `user/message` carries
`data.source.kind`: `user` is a human turn, while `dsh-mnemon`,
`runtime-

context`, `time-context`, `skill-catalog` and `tool-jobs` are
injections. Only kinds listed in `user

SourceKinds` (default `["user"]`) are
indexed, and `assistant/message` contributes `text` blocks onl

y — reasoning is
never searchable.
- **Paragraph units.** A message is split at blank lines (and lon

g paragraphs at
line boundaries) before indexing, so a snippet points at one paragraph rather
than a

whole message.
- **Fast warm path.** The first search builds a derived SQLite index (one table of
m

essage rows); later searches only re-read sessions whose revision changed.
- **Marks in the result l

ist.** Query terms are wrapped in `<mark>` inside the
sidebar rows.
- **Opens at the match.** After

a result is opened, the transcript scrolls to the
matched message and flashes it; older pages are pu

lled first, up to
`revealAttempts` times, and it quietly stays put when the text cannot be found.

pplication directory is touched, so a
harness update cannot eat the plugin.

## Configuration
Every field is optional; the bundle's `cordis.patch.yml` carries the same defaults.
| Field | Default | Meaning |

| `path` | `<dataHome>/storages/session-keyword-search/index.db` | Derived SQLite index. |
| `dataHo

me` | `$DSH_HOME`, else `~/.dsh` | Base directory for the default path. |
| `takeover` | `auto` | `o

ff` leaves the host's own search untouched (and never builds an index). |
| `includeToolEvents` | `f

alse` | Also index `tool/call` and `tool/result` text. |
| `injectedPrefixes` | built-in list | Lead

ing text that marks a machine-injected user message. |
| `injectedPatterns` | `[]` | Extra regular e

xpressions (source strings) treated the same way. |
| `excludeSessionIds` | `[]` | Sessions that mus

t never enter the index. |
| `snippetChars` | `240` | Snippet length in code points. |
| `maxTokens`

| `8` | Query token budget. |
| `refreshDebounceMs` | `5000` | Minimum gap between two corpus recon

ciliations. |
| `uiHighlight` | `true` | Mark query terms inside sidebar result rows (browser enhanc

ement). |
| `uiReveal` | `true` | Scroll to the matched message after a result is opened. |
| `revea

lAttempts` | `20` | How many older-page pulls the reveal may attempt. |
| `userSourceKinds` | `["use
r"]` | `source.kind` allow-list for human turns; injections stay out of the index. |

## How it stays compatible

- Corpus access uses **public services only**: `ctx.sessionQuery.listSessions()`,
`ctx.sessionQuery.

readSession(id)`, and the optional `ctx.sessionPersistence.stat(id)`
revision. The plugin never lear

ns where session logs live, never decodes the
zstd log format, and never parses paths.
- It augments

the live `sessionQuery` instance (`ctx.effect` restores the original
methods on dispose) instead of

replacing the service row, so an incompatible
harness keeps its own behaviour instead of failing to

boot.
- Every search degrades through three stages: **our index → the original provider
→ session-t

itle/workspace substring**, and records the failure for the settings
panel.
## Settings panel

`Settings → Session keyword search` shows the index path, session/message counts,
indexed text size,

the last sync counters, the last error, and offers
**Rebuild** / **Delete index** / **Refresh**. It

talks to the host over the
`/dsh-session-keyword-search` RPC channel.

Channel registration is recorded in `rpc-registration.json` next to the index. If
the panel reports

`HTTP 405`, read that file first: it states whether `connection`
and `webServer` were visible, wheth
er the route registered, and why it failed.
The panel is not required for maintenance:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Verification

`scripts/verify.mjs` is a standalone harness: it feeds the indexer from the
on-disk store and prints

the hits for a set of queries, so recall can be checked
without a running harness.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Measured on a real profile (106 sessions, 48.5k events): 2,114 indexable
messages, 1.25 MB of text,
full cold build ≈ 2.5 s, warm queries 16–60 ms.

Inside a live harness, one boot-time probe reports what the plugin sees through
the **real** service
s and writes it to `%TEMP%/dsh-session-keyword-search-selftest.json`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Known limits

- A session's last turn or two may not be on disk yet, so a just-written message
can be missing unti

l the harness flushes.
- Sessions written before `data.source` existed are treated as human turns (a

n empty
`userSourceKinds` list disables the allow-list).

DOM contracts (`[role="treeitem"]`,
